messages:
maya: FYI - putting together a short playbook for a zero-touch onprem onramp. want to sync on what netops preflight checks we should require.

sam: love this. main asks from field so far: IP reservation patterns, egress NAT expectations, and a clear operator upgrade path. customers keep asking for a non-disruptive patch flow.

olivia: +1. also need an explicit checklist for 'customer-managed load balancer' vs 'operator-provided ingress' cases. those change the firewall and DNS expectations a lot.

jack: question: should the onramp assume an operator-daemonset runs with hostNetwork? some large customers reject hostNetwork for security.

maya: good call. draft option A (operator w/o hostNetwork, requires port-forwarding) and option B (hostNetwork with privileged K8s role). we should surface tradeoffs in the playbook.

emily: netops-side preflight items I want in the runbook: CIDR block reservation sample, AS path for BGP handoff (if applicable), cert distribution steps, and a connectivity smoke test script.

sam: can we add a small `preflight.sh` that the field can run and paste output into support ticket? something like:
```
#!/bin/bash
curl -sS https://metadata.internal/compute || echo "metadata-fail"
nc -zv $LB_HOST 443 || echo "lb-closed"
iperf3 -c ${TEST_IP} -t 5 || echo "throughput-fail"
```
this would catch basics.

olivia: yes — please keep the script read-only and print human-friendly remediation steps. also include a K8s `kubectl` manifest snippet to check operator CR status.

maya: noted. another product decision: require operator auto-upgrades vs manual. my proposal: default to manual for first GA, with an opt-in auto-upgrade toggle for Dedicated/private customers. keeps initial risk lower.

jack: agree on manual default. but include a documented rolling upgrade procedure: steps for canary label, paxos-stable leader drain, and KV cache warmup window. e.g.,
```
1) label nodes: `kubectl label node node-1 onramp=canary`
2) deploy canary: `kubectl apply -f operator-canary.yaml`
3) watch logs: `kubectl -n redwood logs -f operator-canary`
```

emily: for customer-managed networking, we should provide template BGP configs for Arista/Cisco and a minimal Layer-3 NAT example. many customers just want a copy/paste they can hand to netops.

maya: good. add a short section on fallback policies: if private operator loses access to external model catalog, the runtime should gracefully switch to pinned model bundle stored locally. call out the storage sizing and checksum validation steps.

sam: launch criteria proposal: (1) preflight script + smoke tests documented, (2) operator upgrade doc + rollback playbook, (3) three reference customer validations in different network topologies (on-prem isolated, VPC with NAT, cloud-connected via BGP), (4) support runbook and sample BGP configs.

olivia: +1. also require an audit log of handshake events (peering up/down, cert rotates) for compliance customers.

jack: one more ask — include a tiny troubleshooting matrix for common failure modes: DNS misconfig, MTU mismatches, TLS handshake errors with KMS. one-liners for probable causes and first checks.

maya: will draft the playbook this week and post a doc link. tagging @deploy-bot to trigger a checklist item for eng-qa on reference validations.

deploy-bot: [automation] created ticket PROD-ONRAMP-542 in eng-qa for "reference validations: zero-touch onramp" assigned to sam. due 2024-06-05.

emily: thanks — once ticket lands we can schedule the first field run with acme corp next week.

maya: perfect. i'll put a short timeline in the doc: draft by Fri, internal review Mon, field validation sprint Wed. anyone want to add anything else before i post the doc?

sam: add a short section describing the expected SLAs during canary (latency, error budget) and the telemetry hooks we need from the runtime to detect regressions.

olivia: add a note about RBAC: customer tenants must be able to restrict operator impersonation. include example policies.

maya: will include both. thanks all.
